prompt_en: Photorealistic underwater archaeological documentary photograph. A wide, low three-quarter underwater survey frame shows an unmistakably adult underwater archaeologist in a clear observation helmet, recording a drowned lakeside street on a waterproof survey slate. Through the faceplate, the visible adult face has long near-black softly waved hair, warm brown eyes, softly defined brows, fine black eyeliner, and muted coral lips. A continuous drowned settlement rests in place beneath the lake: a submerged settlement with in-situ architecture. Multiple structures form a readable street courtyard or room arrangement across the wide lakebed frame. Walls and thresholds remain attached to foundations embedded in sediment beneath controlled survey lights. Several wall returns floors thresholds or street edges remain connected from a foreground junction to distant foundations. Water sediment aquatic growth and depth cues occupy the architecture under angled late-day caustics and cold blue-green haze. An adult diver ROV or scale marker makes settlement dimensions legible; here, the archaeologist and repeated distance marks supply scale. The survey lights become one continuous luminous measuring chain that traces the original street plan. The chain links the near foundation junction to aligned doorways and distant walls. Distance marks turn the diver into a precise scale cue. First, the archaeologist establishes near scale. Second, the light chain follows the street. Finally, joined foundations reveal a neighborhood. Wide low framing layers the site. Caustics strike during slate notation. Quiet open water isolates the plan. Silt and algae cling to masonry. Distance marks reward a second reading. The measuring chain makes foundation distances and alignments legible.
